evidence: Policy: task tests/scoring.toml:1-11 is '[gates] render = 0.0, constraints = 0.0; [weights] functional 0.6, polish 0.2, visual 0.2; [floors] functional = 0.05'. SHA256 of task scoring.toml (95F70D6E...BBBA), test.sh (BD682592...5AA), tools/score.py (13DE2B38...C04E), restart_mcp.py, Dockerfile and .dockerignore are byte-identical to the frozen template, so no shared harness or reward policy was altered. Gates carry no reward mass: score.py:46 'weighted = sum(w * scores[k] for k, w in weights.items()) / sum(weights.values())' iterates only [weights]; gate scores are used only as thresholds at score.py:41 'gates_passed = all(scores[k] > floor ...)'. Gate judge.toml files use aggregation = "all_pass" with single binary criteria (hro_gate_render, hro_gate_shared); their weight = 1.0 is intra-suite and never enters the reward. Gates apply before shaping: test.sh:212-221 runs 'run_suite gates 1500' then score.py; exit 1 ('1) exit 0') stops before 'run_suite scored 11100' (test.sh:224), so the scored suite is skipped; test.sh:60-61 writes the zero record and traps ensure_reward on every path; test.sh:212 removes any stale scored/ before gates. score.py:42 'scored_ran = gates_passed and scored_data is not None' and :48 'reward = ... if gates_passed and floors_passed else 0.0'. Executed the exact frozen score.py (python 3.12, scratch log dirs, no Docker) against synthetic RewardKit outputs; log saved to per-row-review/evidence/43/score_py_simulation.txt: render gate fail with perfect scored -> exit 1, reward 0.0, scored tests 'skipped'; constraints gate fail -> exit 1, reward 0.0; gates pass but scored missing -> reward 0.0; functional 0.04 with polish/visual 1.0 -> weighted 0.424 but reward 0.0 (floors_passed 0); functional exactly 0.05 -> reward 0.0 (strict '>'); functional 0.06 + polish/visual 1.0 -> 0.436; functional-only perfect -> 0.6; all perfect -> 1.0. Floor magnitude: functional judge.toml has 43 binary criteria summing to weight 58.5, so the floor requires more than ~2.93 weight units of observed functional outcomes. An app that passes only the cheap gates (sign-in, job create, candidate add with independent readback) would typically earn hro_add_candidate 0.5 + hro_job_open 0.5 (only if validation is also right) + hro_candidate_linked 0.5 + hro_restart 1.5 = at most ~3.0/58.5 and often less, i.e. at or below the floor, matching the internal annotation 'passing only the cheap gates earns little'. Each scored prompt also restates the in-dimension gate (functional: 'gives every binary criterion 0'; polish: 'gives binary0 throughout'; visual: 'minimum raw Likert score 1, which normalizes to zero'), so a shell that somehow reached the scored suite still earns nothing in polish/visual. Adversarial cases tried: (1) broken app that could pass: a pretty, gate-passing app with real shared job/candidate storage but no moves/rules/conversations scores functional ~0.009-0.05 -> zeroed by the floor; a variant adding three one-stage/reorder behaviours (~4 units, functional ~0.07) clears the floor and could collect visual up to 0.2, but it is a partially working, server-backed app, so partial credit is the intended shaping, not dead-app farming; polish rows all require live updates, failed-send handling or session resume and therefore cannot be farmed by a non-working app. (2) conforming alternative that could fail: a correct app whose gate judge hits a tool failure gets reward 0 - this is an evaluator-reliability concern owned by gate rows, not a reward-mass defect; template policy is fixed and must not be edited here. Risk=true solely because runtime evidence is missing: raw-evidence-index.json states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent', so no full configured verifier run has shown a real gate failure skipping the scored suite inside the verifier image, and no weak-app run measured where actual near-dead apps land relative to the floor. The score.py simulation is a source-level/unit execution, not a configured judge run, Oracle grade or portal result.
